AN ORDINANCE TO PROTECT THE PUBLIC HEALTH, SAFETY AND GENERAL WELFARE BY ESTABLISHING REGULATIONS RELATING TO THE OPERATION, CONTROL, AND MANAGEMENT OF CEMETERIES OWNED BY THE CITY OF HAZLEHURST, GEORGIA; TO PROVIDE PENALTIES FOR THE VIOLATION OF SAID ORDINANCE; AND TO REPEAL ALL ORDINANCES, AS WELL AS ANY AMENDMENTS THAT MAY HAVE BEEN MADE A PART OF ANY PREVIOUS ORDINANCE.

WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 1.13 (27) of the Charter of the City of Hazlehurst, Georgia, the City of Hazlehurst has the authority to promulgate regulations, rules and other restrictions relating to the operation of municipal cemeteries owned and controlled by the City of Hazlehurst.

WHEREAS, the Mayor and City Council have determined that the current regulations governing the management and operation of municipal cemeteries are inadequate to protect the public health, safety, and general welfare; and

WHEREAS, the Mayor and City Council have discussed and considered such comprehensive rules and regulations and have determined that it is in the best interests of the City to amend the Code of Ordinances by deleting Chapter 3 in its entirety and replacing it with the following rules and regulations relating to the management and operation of the City’s municipal cemeteries;
1: COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF HAZLEHURST, GEORGIA THAT CHAPTER 3 AND ANY AMENDMENTS OF THE EXISTING CODE OF ORDINANCE BE AMENDED AND REORDAINED AS FOLLOWS:

7: Title: This article shall be known as and may be cited as the “City of Hazlehurst Cemetery Ordinance.”

11: It shall be unlawful for any person to bury any dead human body or portion of a human body except in a public or private cemetery within the corporate limits of the City.

CEMETERY LOTS SUBJECT TO RULES AND REGULATIONS; AUTHORITY OF CITY COUNCIL e All cemetery lots owned and purchased within the cemeteries owned by the City of Hazlehurst, shall be subject to the restrictions, covenants, rules and regulations contained within this chapter and shall be subject to such other rules, regulations, amendments or alterations and ordinances as shall be adopted and regularly passed by the City from time to time. A reference to such rules and regulations in the deed or certificate of ownership shall have the same force and effect as if fully set forth therein.

e ‘The City Council shall be responsible for the management, operation, maintenance, and general supervision of all municipal cemeteries and shall have full authority to delegate said responsibility to the City Clerk or City Manager.
14:
e Duties of City Clerk:

e Supervision of Sale of Burial Rights: The City Clerk shall generally supervise the sale and conveyance of burial rights purchased in the public cemeteries of the City. The City Clerk shall prepare a “Cemetery Deed” to be signed on behalf of the City by the Mayor and City Clerk and shall attach the City Corporate Seal to said deed as evidence of its validity.

e Maintenance of Registers: The City Clerk shall be responsible for the maintenance of the Register of Cemetery Deeds and Burials and the Register of Cemetery Rules.

e Issuance of Permits: The City Clerk shall be responsible for the issuance of permits and fees required by this Ordinance.

e Remittance of Payments: The City Clerk shall keep full and detailed accounts of the receipts and expenditures of the municipal cemeteries and shall deposit all monies collected on such accounts upon receipt.
15:
SURVEY REQUIRED; RECORDING BURIALS ON MAP OR SURVEY; REGISTER OF CEMETERY RULES e Registration of Cemetery Deeds and Burials: The City Clerk shall be responsible for keeping a permanent register of all Cemetery Deeds and burials for each deed in all City owned cemeteries, such register shall be known as the REGISTER OF CEMETERY DEEDS AND BURIALS.

e Map or Survey Required: The City Council shall cause to be prepared a map or survey of all city cemeteries and said map or survey shall be maintained in the Office of the City Clerk.

e Recording Burials on Map or Survey: The City Clerk shall be responsible for maintaining the maps or surveys of all city cemeteries and shall mark on such map or survey the name of the lot owner for each particular lot.

D. Maintaining Record of Rules. The City Clerk shall maintain a Register of all

Cemetery Rules that are created pursuant to this Ordinance which shall be known as the REGISTER OF CEMETERY RULES and shall be available to the public.

Certain Rights and Privileges Reserved by City: The following rights and privileges and hereby expressly reserved by the City in its conveyance of any cemetery lot or space. At any time and from time to time, the City may:

e Resurvey, enlarge, diminish, re-plat, alter in shape or size or otherwise change all or any part, portion or subdivision of the property mapped and platted.

e File amended maps or plats thereof and use the same for the erection of buildings or for any purposes or uses connected with, incident to, or convenient for the care, preservation or preparation, for the disposal or interment of dead human bodies, or other cemetery purposes, together with easements and rights of way over and through such premises for the privilege of installing, maintaining, and operating pipelines, conduits or drains for sprinklers, drainage, electric or communication lines, or for any other like purposes.

General Maintenance: Cemeteries owned by the City of Hazlehurst are not perpetual care cemeteries and the City is under no obligation to maintain any set standard for care and upkeep, although the City does currently provide for general maintenance and care of the cemetery grounds.

No Liability for Actions of Lot Owners: The City shall not be held liable for errors or damages which may occur as a result of improper or misinterpretation of instructions from Lot Owners, their heirs, family members, legal representatives, funeral directors, grave excavators, vault installers, memorial and monument dealers, or others acting on behalf of any Lot Owner. The City has the right, without prior approval of the Lot Owner or legal representative, to correct errors made in good faith in any phase of Cemetery administration, operation, or maintenance, without incurring liability of any kind whatsoever.

No Liability for Actions of Others: The City shall take reasonable precaution to protect Lot Owners and the burial rights of Owners within the cemeteries. However, the City disclaims and shall not be liable or responsible for any loss or damage caused by flooding, fire, windstorm, other causes deemed an Act of God, thieves, vandals, malicious mischief makers, explosions, or unavoidable accidents, whether the damage be direct or collateral.

Right of Exceptions: Special cases may arise in which the literal enforcement of a tule or regulation may impose unnecessary hardship. The City reserves the right to make exceptions, suspensions or modifications of any of these rules and regulations without notice when, in the judgment of the City, exercised in the

5

discretion of the City Manager or City Clerk, such action appears necessary. Any such temporary exception, suspension, or modification shall in no way be construed as affecting the general application of these rules and regulations, and shall not act as a waiver of any of the provisions herein. The City will make a written record of any such exception or modification and duly record it in the Register of Cemetery Rules.

The City reserves the right to make any changes deemed necessary as to grading, roads, utility lines and such similar work without notice or approval of any Owner; and to remove or trim any tree, plant or shrub within the cemeteries in the interest of maintaining safety and proper appearance and use of the cemeteries.

The City reserves the right to adopt, amend or suspend any Cemetery rules and/or regulations, at any time, without notification to any Owner but such shall be entered in the Register of Cemetery Rules..

The City shall not be responsible for the loss of any plantings or decorations or any damage to memorials by any cause whatsoever.

Ownership Construed: Ownership of a lot consists only in the ownership of a License for the right of exclusive interment and does not convey fee simple title to the property, such remaining in the City.

Use and Division: Cemetery lots can be used only for interment and for no other purpose and shall not be divided into smaller portions than originally described in the License to the lot.

Reversion to City: Should the owner of a cemetery lot die without devise of the License or any known next of kin, ownership to such License shall revert to the City for the protection of those who may be interred therein.

Recording of License: The holder of any License hereunder shall be entitled but not required to record such License in the deed records of Jeff Davis County, Georgia, such recording shall be only for purposes of evidence of such License should the City’s records be destroyed.

21: There shall be no easement rights granted by the City to any cemetery lot in any road, drive, alley, or walk within a cemetery, but such road, drive, alley or walk may be used for such purposes as long as the City devotes said access points to that purpose.

Cemetery grounds are considered sacred and a strict observance of accepted decorum shall be required at all times. Visitors will use the walks and roads provided at their own risk. The City shall not be liable for any injury or damage incurred by any person or property upon cemetery grounds.

No unleashed pets, food, firearms (other than those carried by duly licensed persons, certified law enforcement officers or military honor officers duly authorized) shall be permitted in City cemeteries at any time.

It shall be unlawful for any person to interfere with the proper conduct of a funeral or with the burying or exhuming of a body or the remains or cremains thereof in the City cemeteries, unless specifically authorized by order of a court of competent jurisdiction.

No person shall drive any vehicle within the cemeteries except upon the driveways prepared and designated for that purpose, and such vehicles shall not be operated in excess of the lower of the posted speed limit or 15 mph.

It shall be unlawful for any person to desecrate or injure the cemeteries, or any Lot, grave, tomb, gravestone, monument, fence, tree, shrubbery or other improvement, fixture or item therein, or to injure or disturb any wildlife within the

Cemetery.

No sale or solicitation of any type on shall be permitted on City cemetery property.

City cemeteries shall be open for visitation during the following hours, unless otherwise posted: Between one-half hour after sunup and one-half hour before sundown.

Loitering in city cemeteries is prohibited and the presence of any person in any

city cemetery during prohibited hours shall be prima facie evidence of loitering.

e Compliance with Article: It shall be unlawful for any person to inter dead human bodies or perform any labor of any kind, including but not limited to, the opening and closing of grave sites, within the limits of any cemetery of the city, except in conformity with this article.

¢ Remedies for Noncompliance: In addition to any penalty imposed for a violation of this article, if any person engaged in the opening and closing of grave sites in a city cemetery fails to comply with any of the requirements of this chapter, the city may undertake to perform the necessary corrective action, and if the city so elects, such person shall be billed by the city for the full and necessary expenses incurred by the city in taking such action. Payment of such bill shall be made to the city within ten (10) days of the date thereof.

e Termination or Suspension of Rights: Upon conviction of any violation of this article by any court of competent jurisdiction or upon failure to promptly remit to the city any sums billed pursuant to subsection (b) above and after notice and an opportunity to appear before the city council, any such person engaged in the opening and closing of grave sites shall have all privileges and rights to engage in such activity terminated or suspended, upon such terms and for such period of time as the council, in its discretion, shall determine.
28:
No labor of any kind, specifically including, but not necessarily limited to, the opening and closing of grave sites and placement of monuments, memorials or coping shall be performed in any city cemetery, only under the supervision of city personnel or a licensed

4 ve funeral director and pursuant to the appropriate permit issued by the City.
29: No grave site shall be opened in any city cemetery unless a permit therefor has been issued by the City Clerk. The fee for a permit shall be established by the City Council from time to time. The Permit shall set forth the names and address of the persons responsible for the proper execution of the permit and compliance with the applicable rules, regulations, ordinances and laws that govern the actions permitted.
30:
All interments, disinterments and removals are subject to the orders and laws of the properly constituted governmental authority of the City of Hazlehurst, Jeff Davis County, and the State of Georgia.

The funeral director shall be responsible for confirming with City Hall that the person arranging for the burial of the deceased has a right to such use of the lot and that such lot is not being used beyond its capacity.

All interments shall be in a liner or vault of concrete, steel, fiberglass or other type of material approved for use by the City Council. All cremains must be securely placed in at least the minimum urn approved by the State Crematory Board, or similar regulatory board or agency, before being interred. All cremains must be interred. No cremains may be scattered in the Cemetery.

Construction of any mausoleum or other type of above-ground interment chamber must be approved in advance by the City Council.

No more than the remains or cremains of one body can be interred in any one Lot, except in the case of a mother and stillborn child.

Caskets containing remains, once interred, shall not be opened or removed without an order from a court of competent jurisdiction.

Funeral processions entering the Cemetery shall be under the control of the funeral home in charge of the burial.

At least one licensed funeral director shall be present throughout any burial/interment service.

The City Clerk or the Clerk’s designated staff member must be given at least twenty-four (24) hours advance notice prior to any interment and one week's

9

advance notice given for disinterment or removal unless otherwise ordered by a court of competent jurisdiction.

e No interment in or disinterment/removal of remains from a Lot shall be undertaken until the Lot is identified on the ground and approved by the City.

e Only human remains and cremains may be interred in any cemetery owned by the City of Hazlehurst.
31:
Any person who performs any labor in connection with the opening and closing of grave sites in any City Cemetery, whether for compensation or gratuitously, shall perform such labor in accordance with the following:

e The area immediately surrounding the grave opening and all loose dirt removed from the grave shall be covered by a tarpaulin or other suitable covering and all excess dirt shall be removed from the grave site area and from the cemetery.

e The opening and closing of grave sites shall at all times be carried out in such mamner as to provide the minimum of disturbance to the grave site area and to the cemetery.

e All vehicles, such as trucks, tractors and the like, used in the opening and closing of grave sites shall, at all times, be parked on roadways within the cemetery, except when in actual use in such opening and closing, and such vehicles shall be parked, set up and moved so as to ensure that they will not sink into the area surrounding the grave site. If any sunken areas, tracks or other like blemishes are made, they shall be promptly and completely corrected and filled.

e Any articles removed by any person in opening and closing grave sites, including grave markers, grave stones, monuments, fences and other such articles and materials, shall be promptly and completely replaced by such person. Such person shall be liable for any damage to such articles and materials.

e Purchase Price: The City Council shall fix the price of all cemetery lots owned by the City. The purchase price for rights to Lots will be set by resolution the City Council and may be periodically altered to accommodate increased costs and needed reserve funds for Cemetery maintenance, acquisition and other related purposes.

e Method of Purchase: All rights to cemetery lots shail be sold by the City through the office of the City Clerk and only after payment of the full price fixed for such lot. The City will not accept partial payments or installment payments for cemetery lots.

e Subject to Provisions of Code of Ordinances: Any deed shall be subject to the provisions of this Ordinance, other applicable ordinances of the City of Hazlehurst, and such additional rules, regulations and restrictions as may hereafter be adopted by the City Council.

REPURCHASE; TRANSFER OF TITLE INVALID; LOT MUST BE SOLD FOR PURCHASE PRICE e Purchase by Owner: A Lot shall be purchased by or on behalf of the intended Owner only and shall not be purchased by any person with intent to sell or transfer ownership to any other person for profit.

e City Right of Repurchase: A Lot may not be sold or otherwise transferred by the Owner to any other person without having first provided the City with a written

11

offer to repurchase at the rate originally paid by the owner at time of purchase. The City shall either repurchase the Lot or decline in writing to repurchase within ten (10) days after the Owner offers it for repurchase.

e Transfer of Title Invalid: Any Lot sold, given or otherwise conveyed by any Owner without following the City right of repurchase procedure shall be an invalid transfer and shall not be recognized by the City for any purpose. Provided, however, Lots may be freely transferred among immediate family members without regard to the City’s repurchase right.

e Lot Must Be Sold for Purchase Price: No sale or transfer of title from one lot owner to another of or to any cemetery lot or part of a lot shall be effective unless such transfer was made at the same purchase price that the lot was originally purchased from the City. The transferee shall be required to produce a bill of sale evidencing the purchase price prior to the City recognizing the transfer of said lot.
40: Where there are several owners of the rights of interment in a cemetery lot, they may designate one or more persons to represent the cemetery lot and file written notice of designation with the City Clerk. In the absence of such notice or of written objection to its so doing, the City is not liable to any owner for interring or permitting an interment or refusing an interment in the cemetery lot upon the request or direction of any co-owners of the cemetery lot. All co-owners of any lot shall be considered as joint tenants with right of survivorship to the License.
44:
Owners of existing cemetery lots shall have the right to erect proper stones or monuments marking the burial site subject to the following provisions:

e All occupied Lots are required to have a minimum of a 2'x1'x4" pillow marker with the name of the deceased, date of birth and date of death. All grave markers in the Cemetery shall be of granite, marble, bronze or other material approved by the City Council, and shall be installed under the direction of a licensed memorial dealer. The City Clerk staff will provide reasonable assistance to licensed

- 7) dh memorial dealers in locating Lots.

No slab shall be set other than in a horizontal position and all corner posts shall be flush with the ground with markers being no more than 6”x 6”.

No monument or family name marker can exceed 14 feet in length or 10 feet in height including the base.

No community mausoleums (12 to 60 crypt units) shall be constructed in any of the City’s municipal cemeteries.

No mausoleum can exceed 10 feet in height and all mausoleums shall be approved by the City Council before any foundation is poured or mausoleum erected.

All mausoleums shall have an Ensure-A-Seal and it shall be the responsibility of the Funeral Director to give the City certification that Ensure-A-Seal was used on the mausoleum. This certification shall be attached to the City’s copy of the cemetery deed.

All stones or markers in the Cemetery are required to have a concrete foundation, which shall be poured under the direction of a licensed memorial dealer.

All stones, markers, slabs, coping, etc. shall not exceed the boundaries of the Owner's Lot(s), unless specifically approved in writing by the City.

Slabs and coping are permitted except in the Hazlehurst Memorial Cemetery. Coping is permitted in the Hazlehurst Memorial Cemetery only when used to join graves together with concrete and rock. All installations much have concrete under the rock.

Memorial dealers shall be responsible and pay for any damages that may occur in the course of monument installation.

The City is not liable for any damages which may occur to such slabs or coping in the regular maintenance of the Cemetery. The City shall not be responsible in any manner for the preservation and care of any memorials installed at the Cemetery.
46:
A permit is required for the installation, removal, or repair of any monument, marker and/or coping within the city cemeteries. The party responsible for installation shall make application for a permit at City Hall. The fee for a permit

13

shall be established by the City Council from time to time. The Permit shall set forth the names and address of the persons responsible for the proper execution of the permit and compliance with the applicable rules, regulations, ordinances and laws that govern the actions permitted.

All improvements or alterations of individual property in the cemeteries shall be not be permitted unless notification has been provided to the City, and should such be made without the required permit, the City may remove such improvements or alterations and person responsible for such actions shall be liable to the City for all expense incurred by the City in removing such improvements or alterations.
47:
General Care: Cemeteries owned by the City of Hazlehurst are not perpetual care cemeteries and the City is under no obligation to maintain any set standard for care and upkeep. At this time, care is assumed by the City and includes the cutting of grass, debris removal, and periodic pruning of shrubs and trees in the common areas, but not within the area of any Lot. Lot Owners are expected to and shall maintain their Lots. The City is under no obligation to maintain any set standard for care and upkeep of the City cemetery grounds.

Grave Decorations:

e Flowers: The placing of cut or artificial flowers over individual graves shall be permitted subject to the following provisions:

e The City shall not be responsible for the care of such flowers or the containers that they are placed in;

e The City shall have the authority to remove, without notice, all flowers, real or artificial, when they fade and/or begin to look tattered.

e Flower Vase or Concrete Pot: Flower vases and concrete pots are permitted in City cemeteries provided that said item must be attached or cemented to the slab or monument and the flowers must be placed inside the container.

Monuments: The record owner of the License shall be responsible for maintaining any monument on the licensed lot. Should the City determine that

If the owner does neither, then the City may, at its sole option, remove, repair or replace such deficient monument and assess the expense thereof against said owner.

e Rubbish; Debris: It shall be unlawful for any person to dispose of any rubbish, trash, waste materials, litter, or debris of any kind in any city cemetery unless the City of Hazlehurst has provided bins for the disposal of such items.

e Trees, Shrubs, and Flowers: It shall be unlawful for any person to plant any tree, shrub, or other plant in any city cemetery or to cut down, injure, break, or destroy any tree, shrub, or other plant growing in the cemetery or to pick, pluck, or cut any flower or decorative plant except as authorized by cemetery rules.

e Loose Decorations: Jt shall be unlawful for any person to place loose decorations, what-nots, trinkets, glassware, toys, or other like items on any slab or monument within the City cemeteries.

e Statues and Benches: It shall be unlawful for any person to place or cause to be placed any concrete statues or benches on or around a grave.

e Grass Removal: It shall be unlawful for any person to remove or cause to be removed the grass or sod from a cemetery lot unless said grass is being removed for the express purpose of installing concrete and rock.

e Signs, Notices, or Advertising: No person shall bring into the cemetery or display therein any signs, notices, advertisements of any nature or kind.
52:
e The City may prosecute any violations of this Ordinance by issuance of a City ordinance citation, in which case the penalty for a violation shall be a fine of not less than $100.00 and not more than $1,000.00 and may include a jail sentence of up to 90 days in jail for each day the violation continues as each day shall be considered a separate offense as set forth in Section 1-6 of the City’s Code of Ordinances.

e Upon issuance of any such citation, the City Manager or Clerk shall be authorized to delay any planned funeral or burial service or the installation of any monument, memorial or other material pending final court determination of the violation.

e No provision of this Section shall be construed to impair any common law or statutory cause of action or legal remedy against any person for injury or damage arising from any violation of this Ordinance or from other law.
53: Should any Section or provision of this Ordinance be declared by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unconstitutional, such decision shall not affect the validity of the Ordinance as a whole nor any part thereof other than the part so declared to be invalid or unconstitutional, and the remainder shall continue in full force and effect.
54:
All Ordinances and parts of Ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby repealed.
